Title: Time series analysis of GSS bonds: Part 1 – Introductory analysis of S&P Green Bond Index
Authors: D Dey; IFoA Data Science, Sustainability, & Climate Change Working Party
Key_Topics: Time series analysis; Green bonds; S&P Green Bond Index; Neural networks (DNN, CNN, LSTM, GRU); XGBoost decision tree; Machine learning; Predictive modeling
Summary: This paper presents an introductory time series analysis of the S&P Green Bond Index using machine learning techniques. The analysis examines neural network architectures (DNN, CNN, LSTM, GRU) and XGBoost to predict 1-day rolling index values from 31 January 2013 to 17 February 2023. Data was split 70% training, 20% validation, 10% testing. Models used Mean Absolute Error (MAE) loss, Adam optimizer, and L2 regularization with Optuna hyperparameter tuning. Results were inconclusive, with models producing comparable performance to the baseline model (MAPE differences of ~0.1%), suggesting 1-day rolling window lacks sufficient information for material outperformance. Future papers will expand analysis to include stationarity, multivariate analysis, and complex models like CEEMDAN-LSTM and N-BEATS.
